On-Chain Operator. Lesson 11.2, Depeg, protocol and smart-contract cover. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already know a health factor and a stop. A hedge is another written path. It is not a claim that the risk is gone.
Cover protocols sell protection against defined events (a protocol hack, a depeg beyond a threshold).
Read: what's covered (exact wording), exclusions, claim process (who decides, how long), payout asset, and the cover provider's own solvency and contract risk.
Work the example on paper. Cover $50,000 in a lending protocol at 2.5%/yr = $1,250/yr. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. If your risk-adjusted yield there is 4.5%, cover takes more than half of it. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. Worth it for a large, concentrated position; often not for a small, diversified one. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Cover wording and exclusions read. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Claim process and payout asset understood. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Cost compared with the yield it protects. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Name two things to check in cover terms. The answer: Any two: covered events, exclusions, claim process, payout asset, provider solvency.
Check yourself. 2. Cover costs 3%/yr on a 5% yield. Net? The answer: About 2%.
Check yourself. 3. Does cover remove all risk? The answer: No. The cover provider has its own claim, solvency and contract risks.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to evaluate on-chain cover products as insurance: what they pay, when, and what they don't.
